featured_reviews.review_text: I recently underwent a hysterectomy at Shri Namah Healthcare under the treatment of Dr. Munjal Kapadia, and my experience has been excellent. The surgery was handled very smoothly, with no pain or complications, and I did not face any issues related to anesthesia. The hospital provided outstanding services, including a well-curated inhouse diet , attentive nursing staff, and very good housekeeping. I was able to start walking on the second day after surgery, which really boosted my confidence and recovery. With proper guidance from the doctors on post-operative care, my healing process was fast and comfortable. I was able to resume my job from home within 15 days, manage all household work by 4 weeks, and even start traveling to the office by cab. The doctors and staff were extremely patient, supportive, and always ready to answer my questions. Although the diagnostic services here are on the costlier side, I was able to manage them through my company health insurance; otherwise, it may feel expensive. However, if you choose the general ward or twin sharing package or can afford the higher medical expenses, this hospital is truly one of the best choices. The care given is really good.
My mother was admitted here. They give personalized attention and good care.
The doctors are well experienced, attentive and explain you everything properly.
The staff is very helpful when it comes to solving any problem.
You are not allowed to get your food. So, if you are a patient's relative, as a local guide I would suggest don't fall for canteen food. The canteen food mostly offers biscuits and stuff like misal pav vada. 1-2 protein bars which are processed.

There is a seperate menu from which you can order food which offers options like Khichadi and dahi which are decent.
Because, when your relatives is admitted in the hospital neglecting your own health and falling for sugary oily food may not be a good option.

I would suggest they have seperate menu, which you will need to call a number and ask for, there you get better options than the processed food.

There is personalised dietician assigned to each patient. She mostly gives balanced options for the patients. I had seen Marie Biscuit in my mom's diet. I personally don't want my mom to eat biscuits with palm oil in it. So, she switched the snack.
So, if you have special preferences. You can always communicate.

One more suggestion to the hospital.
If you have a room patient's relative mostly gets assigned bed.
But if the patient is in the ICU there is no assigned bed for the patient's relative. Which is mostly offered in some other hospitals. So, that could be added.

Before admission, the doctor clearly informed that for a C-section, a compulsory 3-day hospital stay is required for proper recovery. However, since the hospital continuously handles many patients, the patient was given an early discharge while still charging the full amount.

Overall, a very disappointing service and not recommended. Even giving one star feels too much.

My Honest Experience with This Hospital

I have been at this hospital since the 21st because of my mother’s illness, and this is my genuine experience.

This hospital presents itself as a charitable trust hospital, but sadly, my experience was completely different. It honestly feels like the term “charitable trust” is being used as a marketing tactic to attract needy and vulnerable people, while the actual treatment process is not charitable in nature at all.

Before treatment could even begin, we were asked to deposit a lump sum amount. We agreed and paid immediately because my mother’s treatment was the priority.

On the very first night itself, I purchased medicines and injections worth around ₹15,000 at 9 PM. The very next morning, I was again told to buy more medicines. When I politely asked for clarity on how all the medicines got used within such a short time, instead of receiving a proper explanation, I was spoken to rudely.

As a patient’s family member, asking for clarity, transparency, and proper information is not wrong. We are already under emotional and financial stress, and the least we expect is respectful communication.

Over the next few days, I was repeatedly told to buy more medicines, mostly from a specific medical store, but at the time of discharge, the hospital denied having any connection with that store.

If a hospital is truly working under the name of a charitable trust, then there should be honesty, transparency, compassion, and affordability in the treatment process — not pressure, confusion, and questionable practices.

This was a very disappointing and disturbing experience.👎👎👎👎

Yesterday (22 december 2025) I had an appointment with Dr. Amit Mishra at 8pm.
I reached Satya hospital at 7.30ish since I came directly after work. So I was aware that I would have to wait until 8pm at least.
At first, I waited until 8.20pm (which is already a little late for my 8pm appointment) and asked the receptionist how long would it take? She said that there was another patient before me who still had to go and then it would be my turn.
I waited and waited and then at 9.15pm she tells me that I could visit now!!! When I go upstairs I see 5 other people standing there.. and confirm from the nurse if they're waiting in line. She says yes there are 3 or 4 patients to be attended to before my turn.
I wonder how long more it would have taken because I informed the receptionist to cancel my appointment and walked out of the hospital!
The whole idea of taking appointments is so that people are aware of the time they have to be there at. It's very disrespectful to keep people waiting without giving any valid reason. I would have understood if there was any emergency that was being attended to but again it should be communicated properly. Please make sure to have a better organization system or don't take too many patients if you can't handle it time wise.. Or just cancel the whole appointment format and keep it walk in! I'm really very disappointed and frustrated with my first time experience here to have waited for almost 1 hour 15 mins (only including time since appointment time schedule)
